positions.name: GateRationale
positions.frame: what necessitates the signed-manifest requirement for Meridian deployments?
positions.why: The directive (a signed manifest is now required before any Meridian deploy ships) and the assertive that follows it (two unsigned artifacts reached staging last quarter, and that incident is named as the whole reason) read as one directional unit: the rule and its stated cause. Quinton is animator, author, and principal for both — the requirement is true because of the incident it describes, not merely asserted.

positions.name: GateSpecification
positions.frame: what are the operational parameters — requirement, scope, and ownership — of the Meridian deployment gate?
positions.why: Three structured, bullet-labeled assertions (Gate / Scope / Owner) form the governance record of the same gate: what it requires, where it applies, and who holds it. They cohere as one specification read even though footing differs across them — the Gate line still carries Quinton as principal (restating his directive in record form), while Scope and Owner carry no principal, marking them as Xena's own framing decisions rather than attributed statements. That tension — part attributed, part authored — sits inside the one record without resolving.
